format: JIMMY JOHN'S Restaurant at a traditional location (leased, including initial real estate lease costs)

invest.quote: The total investment necessary to begin operation of a JIMMY JOHN'S® Restaurant at a traditional location is $366,200 to $733,500 (including initial real estate lease costs). This includes $5,000 to $39,400 that must be paid to the franchisor or affiliate.

fee.note: $12,500 (or $5,000 for an existing franchisee in good standing) for a Traditional Restaurant previously operated and closed within the last year; $17,500 for Non-Traditional Locations. Initial training for 2 people included; $1,000 per week per additional trainee. Development Agreement: $10,000 per Restaurant, balance of the franchise fee due at signing of each Franchise Agreement. Fees charged in fiscal 2025 ranged from $0 to $35,000.

royalty.quote: Royalty 6% of Restaurant's weekly Gross Sales2 Due on Wednesday of each week on Gross Sales during previous week ending Tuesday

adFund.quote: Advertising and Development Fund Up to 4.5% of Restaurant's weekly Gross Sales (currently the full 4.5%) or 2.25% for Non-Traditional Locations ... Cooperative Advertising Programs Up to 2% of Restaurant's Gross Sales
adFund.note: Currently 4.5% (2.25% for Non-Traditional Locations); cooperative advertising up to 2%. Standard and Strategic incentive programs (signed by March 31, 2027) give a $125,000 or $175,000 Royalty credit per new Restaurant and reduced fund contributions.

otherRecurring.name: Regional Advisory Council
otherRecurring.amount: Council Assessments, when billed (amount varies among councils)

transferFee.amount: $12,500 if transfer is of Restaurant, or controlling ownership interest in you or your owners, and transferee is not an existing JIMMY JOHN'S Restaurant franchisee that has operated at least 1 JIMMY JOHN'S Restaurant for 1 full year ($7,500 for such an existing franchisee; $2,500 for immediate family; $1,000 for non-controlling interest)

special: Royalty and fund contributions are computed and paid weekly. Investment assumes leased premises and excludes real estate purchase or building construction. New-unit incentives give large Royalty credits ($125,000 Standard Markets, $175,000 Strategic Markets) that lower effective royalty in early years.
issues: Cover says traditional total includes initial real estate lease costs while Item 7 total is labeled excluding real estate purchase costs (consistent: leased, no purchase). The list of Standard and Strategic Markets is not printed in the extracted text.
